title: Wrap setTestFlags in act() when testing hooks via renderHook
answers: Why do I get 'An update to TestComponent inside a test was not wrapped in act(...)' when testing a feature-flag hook?
Do I need act() around setTestFlags in tests?
How to test hooks that depend on OpenFeature flags without React act warnings?
body: Symptom: a test using renderHook() to test a hook that reads a feature flag (e.g. via useFlagX) throws 'An update to TestComponent inside a test was not wrapped in act(...)' when calling setTestFlags. Root cause: renderHook wraps the hook in a hidden TestComponent; setTestFlags fires an OpenFeature change event asynchronously, and the TestComponent's resulting setState happens outside the synchronous call, not inside setTestFlags itself (which only wraps its own internal act). Fix pattern: wrap the setTestFlags call itself in `await act(async () => { setTestFlags(...) })` in tests that use renderHook on a flag-consuming hook — this differs from other call sites of setTestFlags (e.g. full component render tests) which don't need the extra act(). Constraints: only needed for renderHook-based hook tests reacting to flag-change events; not a general rule for every setTestFlags usage.
applies: Unit tests for hooks (via @testing-library/react renderHook) that consume OpenFeature/unleash-style flags via @grafana/test-utils/unstable's setTestFlags.

This differs from other setTestFlags call sites (full component render tests) which don't need the extra act(). Required only for renderHook-based hook tests reacting to flag-change events, using @testing-library/react renderHook and @grafana/test-utils/unstable's setTestFlags.
